approvals_flow: Agent hits a gated tool call -> happy-cli parks it pending (for Claude it is built on the Agent SDK canUseTool callback, which can stay pending indefinitely; for Codex/Gemini it is ACP session/request_permission with the four allow/reject option kinds) [agents: canUseTool semantics; ACP permission model] -> happy-cli encrypts the approval event with device-paired TweetNaCl keys and posts it to happy-server, which stores only ciphertext [prior-art: Happy E2E design] -> server fires a push (Expo push -> APNs/FCM) to the store-distributed Happy app [prior-art: Happy push on permission requests] -> lock-screen notification; user taps, app opens the approvals inbox, fetches and decrypts authoritative pending state (never trusts the push payload) -> user taps Approve / Deny or types a steering reply -> encrypted response returns to happy-cli -> the SDK/ACP callback resolves -> agent resumes. The laptop terminal reflects the same resolution via Happy two-way sync and one-keypress device handoff [prior-art: Happy handoff]. iOS backgrounding is safe: no socket needs to survive, because the pending approval lives on the laptop until answered and the app re-syncs on open [phone: iOS suspends sockets; agents: pending canUseTool]. Fallback lane requiring zero of our infra: `/remote-control` mirrors the session to the Claude mobile app with "Push when actions required" approvals [prior-art: Remote Control].

build_phases.scope: brew install tmux (not currently installed) [terminals: local check]; Tailscale on laptop + iPhone (free Personal plan), disable laptop node key expiry day one, VPN On Demand with *.ts.net trigger [transport]; pmset -c sleep 0 + caffeinate LaunchAgent; enable Tailscale SSH; run `claude remote-control` inside a tmux session (process must stay alive) [prior-art: RC limits]; install Claude mobile app; install Blink Shell, connect mosh/ssh over the tailnet, `tmux attach`.
build_phases.deliverable: Same day: approve/deny/steer Claude Code sessions from the phone with push (Claude app), Dispatch for remote Claude kickoff, and full input/output control of any tmux terminal from the phone via Blink. Laptop reachable 24/7. Zero custom code.

build_phases.phase: Phase 2 — Happy hub on hosted relay (~2 days)
build_phases.scope: Install happy-cli; run `happy daemon start` under a launchd LaunchAgent (state in ~/.happy/daemon.state.json); QR-pair the store-distributed Happy app; use Happy's hosted relay (E2E, ciphertext-only server); explicitly never use `happy connect` API-key storage (the #680 hole) — subscription OAuth stays local; wire up Codex and Gemini (--experimental-acp) as Happy agents; shift habit to launching agents via happy or from the phone.
build_phases.deliverable: One phone app showing all AI-agent sessions: approvals inbox with push, steering messages, live streaming output, remote spawn in any project directory, device handoff. Phase 1 Remote Control demoted to fallback.

build_phases.phase: Phase 3 — Terminals with touch UX + VS Code (~1.5 days)
build_phases.scope: Install VibeTunnel (menu-bar + native iOS app), reachable strictly over Tailscale; set VS Code default terminal profile to `tmux new -A -s vscode-N`; set tmux history-limit and a window-size policy in .tmux.conf before creating sessions; enable `code tunnel` as a LaunchAgent escape hatch.
build_phases.deliverable: Touch-friendly view + control of every tmux terminal including VS Code integrated ones (new terminals get persistence for free); full IDE available from the phone browser via vscode.dev when genuinely needed.

build_phases.scope: Run happy-server (standalone Docker image, no external Postgres/Redis/S3) on the laptop via OrbStack/Docker, bound to localhost, published with `tailscale serve` under the ts.net Let's Encrypt cert (auto-renewed); point happy-cli (HAPPY_SERVER_URL) and the app's custom-server setting at it; verify push delivery from the self-hosted server on-device before cutting over; keep hosted-relay config as fallback.
build_phases.deliverable: Identical UX with no third party in the agent data path: all sync device-to-device over WireGuard, zero public endpoints. If self-hosted push fails verification, stay on the hosted relay knowingly (still E2E).

build_phases.phase: Phase 5 (optional, only if two-app UX grates) — Single-app terminals via Happy fork (~6-8 days)
build_phases.scope: Fork Happy (MIT): add a terminal session type — happy-cli side speaks tmux control mode (`tmux -C attach`, %output streaming, send-keys input, capture-pane -p -e -S - replay, pause-mode flow control) over the existing E2E channel; Expo side renders it in an xterm.js WebView per the @fressh pattern (write coalescing, Ctrl/Esc/arrow key row). First re-verify that Happy still lacks this (absence was UNVERIFIED).
build_phases.deliverable: One app is the single remote for agents AND terminals; VibeTunnel/Blink retired to fallbacks. Deferred by default — this is the only real custom code in the design.

laptop_side: All reused components, glued by dotfiles and launchd plists (the only "code" until optional Phase 5): (1) tmux via Homebrew — the single terminal substrate; .tmux.conf sets history-limit before any session exists and a window-size policy; VS Code's default terminal profile becomes `tmux new -A -s vscode-N` [terminals: tmux is the capture layer; history-limit applies only to new windows]. (2) happy-cli daemon (Node, `happy daemon start`, auto-started by a launchd LaunchAgent as the logged-in user; state in ~/.happy/daemon.state.json) — spawns and manages Claude Code (default), Codex, and any ACP-compatible agent, owns approvals/streaming/remote-spawn [prior-art: happy-cli daemon facts]. (3) happy-server, Phase 4 only: the standalone Docker image (no external Postgres/Redis/S3) on OrbStack/Docker Desktop, bound to localhost and published via `tailscale serve` [prior-art: Happy self-host]. (4) VibeTunnel menu-bar app for touch-friendly terminal access, tailnet-only [prior-art: VibeTunnel]. (5) tailscaled + `tailscale serve` (auto-renewing ts.net LE cert) [transport: cert renewal]. (6) claude CLI on subscription OAuth, with `claude remote-control` inside tmux as the fallback lane; DISABLE_TELEMETRY/DO_NOT_TRACK/custom base URL must stay unset or it silently dies [prior-art: RC limits]. (7) Power config: pmset -c sleep 0 (+ caffeinate LaunchAgent) — hard prerequisite, nothing works if the laptop sleeps [transport pitfall]. (8) Optional `code tunnel` LaunchAgent. Node v26 already present; tmux is not — brew install is step one [terminals: local check].
name: Happy-on-Tailnet
not_built: Custom phone app, APNs pipeline, Apple Developer account, TestFlight re-upload churn — Happy, VibeTunnel, Claude, Blink are store-distributed apps whose maintainers carry the $99/yr + push-entitlement burden [phone: paid account mandatory; prior-art pitfall: home-grown app pays it for one user]
Relay server and E2E encryption — happy-server + TweetNaCl device-key pairing reused as-is [prior-art: Happy E2E]
Laptop daemon, Claude Agent SDK integration, ACP client, approvals state machine, session-spawn API — all happy-cli [prior-art: 90% of brief]

VS Code companion extension — research shows extension-side mirroring is best-effort-only anyway (read() attach-at-start, no raw-stream API, webview isolation); tmux default profile + `code tunnel` replace it [vscode facts]

Terminal transport and renderer — no ttyd/GoTTY/tty-share/upterm deployment, no @xterm/headless service, no WebSocket protocol; tmux + VibeTunnel/Blink+mosh cover it [terminals: skip ttyd/GoTTY as components]
Any TUI scraping of agent screens to detect prompts — structured channels only (SDK/ACP via Happy); Omnara's deprecation is the standing warning [prior-art: Omnara]
Public endpoints, Cloudflare Tunnel/Access, bespoke auth/token system — tailnet + Happy QR pairing + Tailscale SSH identity instead [transport: Cloudflare reads plaintext]
Push notification service — Expo->APNs/FCM via Happy's published app; no ntfy piggyback (documented iOS flakiness) [phone: ntfy issues]
Retro-capture of non-tmux PTYs (impossible on macOS; reptyr is Linux-only) — the UI just shows those terminals as not capturable [terminals: fact 6]
Multi-user support, sharing, or any relay hardening beyond single-owner use — out of scope for a personal tool
notifications: Entirely reused: Happy's store-distributed app means APNs/FCM certificates and the $99/yr Apple Developer account are the Happy maintainers' problem — the single biggest cost the glue stance deletes, since a home-grown standalone iOS app cannot have push without the paid program [phone: free accounts have no push entitlement, 7-day builds]. Happy pushes on permission requests and task completion [prior-art: Happy features]; the Claude app pushes for /remote-control sessions ("Push when Claude decides" / "Push when actions required") [prior-art: RC]. Pushes are treated as signals only — the app fetches decrypted authoritative state over its channel, so nothing sensitive rides Expo/APNs in a form third parties can read (Happy payloads are within its E2E design; Expo itself offers no payload E2E) [phone: Expo push transparency]. Two verifications scheduled early on real devices: approval actions from killed state (Android action buttons historically no-op'd) [phone: expo issue history], and push delivery when the server is self-hosted in Phase 4 (assumed from the self-hosting reviewer's report, UNVERIFIED). Escalation if an approval sits unanswered is Happy's behavior to inherit, not ours to build; the guaranteed fallback is always tap-notification -> inbox.
phone_side: iPhone (primary): Happy app from the App Store — Expo/React Native; sessions list, approvals inbox with push, chat-style steering, live streaming, git diff views, remote spawn, device handoff; custom server URL switched to the self-hosted ts.net endpoint in Phase 4 [prior-art: Happy app + self-host reviewer used same apps]. VibeTunnel native iOS app for terminal sessions over Tailscale [prior-art: VibeTunnel remote via Tailscale]. Blink Shell (native mosh) + Tailscale SSH as the raw-terminal fallback that works when everything else is broken [prior-art: Blink/mosh/tmux classic stack]. Claude mobile app for the /remote-control fallback lane and Dispatch kickoff [prior-art: RC facts]. Tailscale iOS app with VPN On Demand *.ts.net hostname trigger (interface rule "Do Nothing") so the tunnel self-raises when any app resolves the ts.net name — no manual VPN toggling, and battery stays fine because the laptop is never an exit node [transport: iOS on-demand + battery facts]. Android parity: Happy ships Android; Termius (mosh via compat library) replaces Blink; Tailscale Android — store installs sidestep the 2026 sideloading verification changes entirely [phone: Android verification timeline]. No custom app is built; if Phase 5 ever happens it is a fork of Happy's existing Expo app, not a greenfield client.
remote_start: From the Happy app: pick a project directory and agent, and the happy-cli daemon spawns the session with no terminal open on the laptop (`happy daemon start/stop/status`, auto-start, state in ~/.happy/daemon.state.json) [prior-art: happy-cli daemon]. Claude sessions spawned this way land in the shared ~/.claude/projects store, so back at the laptop they resume in the CLI with `claude --resume <id>` — with the known constraints: resume is keyed to the encoded cwd, and laptop CLI and daemon must not drive the same session ID concurrently (treat attach as exclusive; concurrency is UNVERIFIED) [agents: session store + resume pitfalls]. Secondary zero-infra path: Claude Dispatch from the Claude mobile app (message a task, Desktop spawns it) [prior-art: Dispatch]. New plain terminal remotely: create a session from VibeTunnel's UI or Blink ssh then `tmux new -A -s name -c ~/project`. Remote spawn is by nature remote code execution on the laptop; the gate is layered reused auth — WireGuard device identity (tailnet) + Happy's QR pairing with device-held keys — and no generic exec endpoint exists beyond what these audited-in-public tools already ship [transport recommendation: typed operations, no public ports].
risks: Happy hosted relay reliability: the public endpoint (api.cluster-fluster.com) has documented timeout episodes — until Phase 4 self-host, a relay outage removes remote agent control (Remote Control and Blink lanes still work) [prior-art: self-hoster's report]

Happy security posture: Discussion #680 showed 'E2E' marketing while `happy connect` API keys were server-decryptable via HANDY_MASTER_SECRET; we avoid that exact hole (no API keys stored, subscription OAuth stays local) but the codebase is not independently audited — self-hosting on the tailnet in Phase 4 is the real containment [transport: Happy #680]

Three load-bearing UNVERIFIED items: (a) Happy lacking plain-terminal sessions (absence unverified — re-check before funding Phase 5), (b) push delivery from a self-hosted happy-server through the store apps (verify before cutover), (c) concurrent CLI + daemon resume of one Claude session (assume single-writer) [prior-art/agents]

Upstream churn: Happy wraps the Claude Code/Codex processes, the exact treadmill that killed Omnara's OSS wrapper — we inherit breakage windows after agent CLI releases and depend on Happy's fix latency instead of owning the maintenance [prior-art: Omnara deprecation]

The 'single remote' brief is met with two apps (Happy for agents, VibeTunnel for terminals); if that UX does not hold up, Phase 5's fork is the exit — and maintaining a fork of a fast-moving Expo monorepo is a real ongoing cost, the one place glue-first can turn into build-anyway

/remote-control fallback is fragile: claude.ai OAuth only, silently disabled by DISABLE_TELEMETRY/DO_NOT_TRACK/custom ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL, directory-bound per server, and transcripts sit on Anthropic servers un-E2E'd [prior-art: RC limits]

The laptop is a single point of failure with no out-of-band recovery: sleep misconfig, power cut, or ISP outage kills everything; pmset + disabled key expiry mitigate the self-inflicted cases only (no remote power control is built)

tmux-only capture is honest but partial: terminals opened outside tmux, or before the VS Code profile change, are permanently invisible (macOS PTY limitation) — the session list must say 'not capturable' rather than pretend [terminals: reptyr not macOS]

Phone tmux attach registers a client size (window-size=latest default) and can shrink laptop panes, and Claude Code's ink TUI demonstrably corrupts on resize — keep agent TUIs viewed through Happy, never through a phone-attached tmux client, and set a window-size policy for shared shells [terminals: ink resize bugs]
First request after VPN idle can time out while WireGuard establishes via the On Demand trigger — expect a retry, not instant connect [transport: on-demand pitfall]
surface_capture: (1) Claude Code sessions — primary: launched/owned by the happy-cli daemon, which drives Claude with structured approvals, streaming, and push; because Claude sessions live in the shared ~/.claude/projects JSONL store, phone-started sessions remain resumable on the laptop with `claude --resume <id>` and vice versa [agents: shared session store; prior-art: happy-cli]. A `claude` the user launches by hand: preferred habit is launching via happy; alternatively that one session uses built-in `/remote-control` to the Claude app (works from CLI and the VS Code extension) [prior-art: RC facts]. A bare Claude TUI inside tmux is still screen-mirrorable as a terminal (VibeTunnel/Blink) but gets no structured approvals — we never scrape the ink TUI, per both researchers' warnings [terminals + agents pitfalls]. (2) Other AI agents — Happy natively supports Codex, agy, and any ACP-compatible CLI, so Gemini CLI via `--experimental-acp` rides the same approvals/streaming pipeline (ACP session/request_permission maps to the same inbox) [prior-art: Happy agents; agents: ACP ecosystem]. Non-ACP agents fall back to a plain tmux terminal, mirror-only, labeled as such. (3) Plain terminals — tmux is the sole capture substrate: any same-user process can attach to the default tmux socket regardless of who started tmux [terminals: fact 5]. Phone access: VibeTunnel (native iOS app, touch UI, tailnet-only) or Blink+mosh then `tmux attach`. Terminals not inside tmux are not capturable on macOS at all (no PTY-master API; reptyr is Linux/FreeBSD only) — the UI shows them as existing-but-not-capturable, honestly [terminals: fact 6 + honesty pitfall]. (4) VS Code itself — no companion extension in this stance: integrated terminals become tmux-visible by setting the default terminal profile to `tmux new -A -s vscode-N` (also giving crash persistence) [terminals recommendation]; the Claude extension chat panel is unreachable by design (webview isolation) so `/remote-control` from the extension is the supported hook [vscode: webview isolation; prior-art]; the full IDE from the phone is the documented escape hatch `code tunnel` -> vscode.dev in the phone browser, kept as a break-glass tool, not a daily surface, given its poor touch UX [vscode: tunnels facts].
thesis: Do not write a platform that a maintained MIT project already ships: Happy (22.9k stars, E2E-encrypted, self-hostable, multi-agent, store-distributed iOS/Android apps) already implements roughly 90% of this brief, so the product is Happy composed with tmux as the universal terminal capture layer, Tailscale as the only network, VibeTunnel/Blink for terminals, and Claude's built-in /remote-control as the zero-infra fallback — custom work is confined to configuration, launchd plists, and (only if the two-app UX fails) an additive terminal-session fork of Happy.
transport: Two layers, both reused. Agent channel: Happy's protocol — TweetNaCl E2E encryption with keys generated on-device, QR one-time-challenge pairing, server stores only ciphertext [prior-art: Happy E2E]; Phases 2-3 it runs through Happy's hosted relay (acceptable interim: payloads sealed, and we never invoke `happy connect` API-key storage, the exact #680 hole — the user's subscription OAuth never leaves the laptop), Phase 4 moves happy-server onto the laptop itself. Network layer: Tailscale free Personal plan (1 user, laptop + phone, well inside limits) [transport: pricing]; the self-hosted server binds localhost and is published only via `tailscale serve` under the laptop's MagicDNS name with an auto-renewing ts.net Let's Encrypt cert — avoiding both the 90-day manual `tailscale cert` trap and iOS ATS exceptions for plain http [transport: cert + ATS facts]; laptop node key expiry disabled day one so it does not silently drop offline at day 180 [transport: key expiry]; phone uses VPN On Demand's *.ts.net hostname trigger (interface rule "Do Nothing") so the tunnel raises automatically [transport: iOS on-demand]. Cloudflare Tunnel was rejected because its edge terminates TLS and reads the plaintext command channel, and a service token in the app is a static bearer credential [transport: CF facts]. Result: zero public endpoints, zero 0.0.0.0 binds, WireGuard device-to-device for everything including SSH/mosh/VibeTunnel, with app-level auth (Happy pairing keys, Tailscale SSH identity) stacked on top.

name: Tether
thesis: One custom TypeScript daemon on the laptop is the single source of truth for everything running there; the phone is a thin Expo client that assumes it is always disconnected and catches up from cursors. Agents are driven only through structured protocols (Claude Agent SDK natively, ACP for everyone else) — never by scraping TUIs (Omnara's deprecation is the cautionary tale) — while tmux is the one capture layer for raw terminals. Transport is Tailscale-direct with zero public endpoints and typed operations only, because this is remote command execution on a personal machine.
laptop_side: A single Node/TypeScript daemon, `tetherd`, installed as a launchd LaunchAgent (must run as the logged-in user or it lands on the wrong tmux socket — terminal research pitfall). Components inside one process: (1) Fastify HTTP + WebSocket server bound exclusively to the laptop's Tailscale 100.x address, fronted by `tailscale serve` for real Let's Encrypt TLS on the ts.net MagicDNS name with automatic cert renewal (raw `tailscale cert` files expire in 90 days unrenewed — transport research). (2) Agent adapter tier 1: Claude via @anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk `query()` with `includePartialMessages` for streaming, `canUseTool` for the approvals inbox, and the `PermissionRequest` hook to trigger push (the SDK docs explicitly recommend this hook for external notifications). Built on `query()` + options only — the V2 createSession API was removed in 0.3.142. (3) Agent adapter tier 2: an ACP client on @agentclientprotocol/sdk spawning Gemini CLI (`--experimental-acp`) and Codex via @agentclientprotocol/codex-acp as stdio subprocesses; the daemon implements ACP's client-side terminal capability so agents' shell commands stream live. Never `codex exec` — it has zero approval prompts. (4) Terminal adapter: one long-lived `tmux -C attach` control-mode client on the default per-user socket (hosted under node-pty); %output notifications octal-decoded to raw bytes, `capture-pane -p -e -S -` for scrollback replay on phone connect, `send-keys` for input, pause-mode flow control (`refresh-client -f pause-after=...`) so a `yarn build` cannot flood LTE. (5) Persistence: better-sqlite3 holding a cursor-addressed append-only event log per session (the reconnect-replay backbone, with includePartialMessages deltas batched before writing), approvals table with expiry, hashed per-device auth tokens, and an audit log of every mutating call. Plus the daemon's own transcript mirror for ACP agents, because ACP session/load cold-recovery is unreliable in practice. (6) Push dispatcher: expo-server-sdk → Expo Push Service, content-free payloads. (7) A thin optional VS Code companion extension (separate install, Phase 4) that connects OUT to the daemon over localhost WebSocket as a sensor/actuator only — the daemon owns everything that must survive VS Code closing.
phone_side: Expo (React Native + TypeScript) app with expo-dev-client from day one — Expo Go cannot receive remote push, and a PWA is disqualified because iOS web push has no action buttons and materially worse delivery than APNs (phone research). Distribution: paid Apple Developer Program ($99/yr, non-negotiable for the push entitlement) + TestFlight internal testing on iOS (90-day re-upload cadence, CI-reminded); EAS-built APK sideload on Android, registering the free 20-device limited-distribution account before the Sept 2026 verification enforcement. App structure: three tabs — Inbox (approvals + AskUserQuestion cards, badge-counted), Sessions (grouped: agents / terminals / IDE, each labeled with capture fidelity), Activity (audit feed). Session detail renders agent streams as a FlashList of parsed message blocks (cheap, selectable, chat-like — not xterm), with an xterm.js-in-WebView view (pattern: @fressh/react-native-xtermjs-webview, rAF + 8KB write coalescing) reserved for real PTY sessions, rendered at the pane's laptop-side size with pan/pinch — the phone NEVER resizes the PTY, since Claude Code's ink TUI demonstrably corrupts on resize. Custom accessory key row for Esc/Ctrl/Tab/arrows. expo-notifications category "approval" with Approve + Deny actions (Deny carries a text-input for a steering reply), interruption-level time-sensitive, `opensAppToForeground:false`. Device token and pairing credential in expo-secure-store behind Face ID. Networking: one WebSocket while foregrounded, torn down on background (iOS suspends within seconds and background URLSession has no WebSocket support), every stream resumed by cursor on foreground — the app never assumes the socket survived.
transport: Tailscale-direct, no relay. Laptop + phone on the free Personal plan (well within 6 users / unlimited devices); daemon bound only to the tailnet interface so home-Wi-Fi devices cannot even reach the port; HTTPS/WSS via `tailscale serve` on `laptop.<tailnet>.ts.net` — real TLS, so no iOS ATS exceptions. iOS VPN On Demand with the *.ts.net hostname trigger (interface rule set to "Do Nothing", the documented requirement) auto-raises the tunnel when the app dials the MagicDNS name; no Tailscale SDK embedding needed since the tunnel is device-wide. Battery is fine because the laptop is never an exit node. Day-one setup: disable Tailscale key expiry on the laptop node (180-day default silently kills it) and pmset to prevent sleep while plugged in. On top of WireGuard: app-level auth via QR pairing on the laptop that hands the phone a per-device random bearer token, stored hashed on the daemon, individually revocable, shown in a device list. The API is typed operations only — approveDecision(approvalId), sendMessage(sessionId), sendKeys(terminalId), startSession(agent, dir ∈ allowlisted roots), attachTerminal(id) — never a generic exec endpoint; terminal attach gets a separate per-session confirmation and all input is audit-logged. Why over Cloudflare Tunnel: Cloudflare's edge reads the plaintext command channel and a baked-in service token is a static bearer credential; why over a self-hosted relay: no internet-facing service to patch, and WireGuard gives device-to-device E2E for free (Happy shipped 'E2E' marketing while server-decryptable API keys sat in its relay — Discussion #680).
surface_capture: Four surfaces, each captured at the highest fidelity actually possible, labeled honestly in the UI. (1) CLAUDE CODE: hosted inside the daemon via Agent SDK `query()` — full structure: canUseTool approvals, includePartialMessages streaming, cwd pinned per session (resume from a different cwd silently forks a fresh session). Because SDK and CLI share ~/.claude/projects, phone-started sessions are resumable at the desk with `claude --resume <id>`; attach is treated as exclusive single-writer — the daemon releases via the defer hook decision before handoff (concurrent dual-writer behavior is UNVERIFIED). Sessions the user runs interactively in a tmux-wrapped terminal appear as terminal mirrors (screen-exact, no structured approvals); sessions inside the VS Code Claude chat panel are invisible — webview isolation makes that a hard wall, and the UI says so rather than pretending. (2) OTHER AI AGENTS: the ACP tier — Gemini CLI natively, Codex via the official codex-acp adapter; session/request_permission's four option kinds and session/update's tool-call lifecycle map 1:1 onto the same inbox and stream model, so every future ACP agent is free. Capabilities (loadSession, resume) are feature-detected at initialize; the daemon's own SQLite transcript mirror covers cold restarts. (3) PLAIN TERMINALS: tmux is the sole real capture layer. Setup installs tmux (not currently on the machine — brew prerequisite), sets history-limit before any session spawns, and switches VS Code's default terminal profile to `tmux new -A -s vscode-N` — after that, every new integrated or Terminal.app shell is fully mirrored (control-mode clients don't affect window sizing, so the phone watches without shrinking the laptop view) and gains crash persistence for free. The daemon can attach to ANY session on the user's tmux socket regardless of who launched tmux. Non-tmux terminals cannot be retro-attached (no macOS API for another process's PTY master; reptyr is Linux-only) — listed as "not capturable" or, in VS Code, downgraded per (4). (4) VS CODE ITSELF: the thin companion extension reports IDE state over stable APIs — workspaceFolders, activeTextEditor, tabGroups, window focus, terminal list with shell type/PID/cwd — and does best-effort mirroring of non-tmux integrated terminals via the shell-integration API (subscribe in onDidStartTerminalShellExecution, call execution.read() immediately; command-scoped, attach-at-start-only) with input via Terminal.sendText(shouldExecute=false) for raw keys. It never builds on onDidWriteTerminalData (forever-proposed, Marketplace-blocked) and never touches the Claude chat webview. Multiple VS Code windows mean multiple extension connections; the daemon namespaces them.
approvals_flow: Agent requests a non-auto-approved tool → the Claude SDK's canUseTool promise pends (or ACP sends session/request_permission) → daemon writes an approval row (id, session, tool name, input summary, diff payload, expiry) to SQLite, appends an event to the session's cursor stream, and the PermissionRequest hook fires the push dispatcher → Expo Push → APNs/FCM as a time-sensitive notification in the "approval" category, payload carrying only IDs (nothing sensitive transits Expo/Apple; 4KB cap is irrelevant). On the phone: lock-screen Approve/Deny buttons handle without opening the app (opensAppToForeground:false) and POST an idempotent, approval-ID-scoped decision over the tunnel; tapping the body deep-links into the inbox card, which fetches the full tool input/diff from the daemon — the guaranteed fallback, since killed-state action taps are the least reliable path on both platforms. "Always allow" maps to updatedPermissions (Claude) / allow_always (ACP); Deny's text-input doubles as a steering message queued to the session. The decision resolves the pending canUseTool promise ({behavior:'allow'|'deny'}) → the agent resumes → stream events flow to any connected client, and the desk view and phone stay in sync because both read the same event log. Robustness: decisions are idempotent with server-side expiry and a confirming state change in the inbox; unanswered approvals re-notify on an escalating schedule (push receipts only confirm handoff to APNs, not delivery); if the daemon must restart with an approval pending, it uses the SDK's defer hook decision and resumes the session rather than losing the prompt. Note the honest gap: canUseTool never fires for auto-approved tools, so a PreToolUse hook feeds those into the Activity feed instead of silently vanishing.
notifications: Laptop daemon → HTTPS POST to Expo Push Service (free, no public endpoint needed on the laptop, median 42ms handoff) → APNs/FCM. Event types: approval needed, AskUserQuestion, session finished, session errored, session idle-waiting, terminal bell (opt-in). All payloads content-free (IDs + generic titles); the app treats every push as a signal and fetches authoritative state on open. iOS uses time-sensitive interruption level (self-service capability, breaks through Focus) with graceful degradation if the user disables it; Android action buttons are tested on-device in week one given their history of killed-state no-ops (fixed in expo PR #35295 but reports continued). DeviceNotRegistered receipts rotate stored tokens; Expo push-security access tokens are enabled and the ExponentPushToken is treated as a secret. Because tickets/receipts never prove device delivery, the in-app inbox remains the source of truth and the daemon escalates unanswered approvals. Silent content-available pushes are never used for sync — foreground catch-up plus visible pushes only.
remote_start: New Task screen on the phone → project picker fed by the daemon from a configured allowlist of project roots (directories outside the allowlist cannot be targeted, by API shape not by validation) → choose agent (Claude / Gemini / Codex), initial prompt, and permission mode → typed startSession call. The daemon spawns: Claude via SDK query() with cwd pinned to the chosen directory (avoiding the cwd-keyed resume trap); ACP agents via session/new on a fresh subprocess; a plain terminal via `tmux new-session -d -c <dir>`, instantly mirrored. The session appears in the Sessions list streaming within seconds, the start is audit-logged, and a finish/needs-input push closes the loop. Claude sessions started this way are later resumable at the laptop with `claude --resume <id>` because SDK and CLI share the on-disk session store — remote start is not a one-way street.

build_phases.scope: Daemon skeleton: Fastify + WS on the Tailscale interface, tailscale serve TLS, SQLite event log with cursor replay, QR pairing with hashed per-device tokens, audit log. Claude tier only: Agent SDK sessions, canUseTool approvals, streaming, remote start in allowlisted dirs. Expo dev-client app: Sessions list, approval inbox, session detail as FlashList stream, New Task screen. Expo Push with Approve/Deny lock-screen actions, time-sensitive, killed-state testing on real devices. TestFlight + EAS Android build. Setup script: Tailscale key-expiry off, pmset, LaunchAgent install.
build_phases.deliverable: Leave the house while a Claude session runs: get a lock-screen push when it needs approval, approve/deny/steer from the phone, watch live output, and kick off new Claude tasks in any allowlisted project remotely. Complete daily-driver for the single biggest pain.

build_phases.scope: tmux control-mode adapter in the daemon (%output decode, capture-pane replay, send-keys, pause-mode flow control), setup step that installs tmux and switches the VS Code default terminal profile to the tmux wrapper, xterm.js-in-WebView terminal screen with write coalescing, pan/zoom at laptop-side pane size, custom Esc/Ctrl/arrow key row, per-session attach confirmation.
build_phases.deliverable: Every tmux-wrapped terminal (all new VS Code terminals post-setup, plus anything started with tmux) is watchable and typeable from the phone with instant scrollback replay — including interactive TUI agents run manually, mirrored screen-exact.

build_phases.scope: ACP client on @agentclientprotocol/sdk with capability feature-detection, Gemini CLI (--experimental-acp) and Codex (codex-acp) adapters, normalization of session/request_permission and session/update into the existing event schema, daemon-side transcript mirror for ACP sessions, client-side ACP terminal capability, agent picker in New Task.
build_phases.deliverable: Gemini and Codex sessions appear in the same Sessions list with the same approvals inbox, push actions, streaming, and remote start as Claude — one inbox for every agent.

build_phases.scope: Thin companion extension: IDE state reporting (workspace, editors, tabs, focus, terminal inventory with shell/cwd), best-effort shell-integration mirroring of non-tmux terminals with honest capability labels, sendText input routing with terminal-identity verification, multi-window namespacing. App polish: device management/revocation screen, escalating re-notify, Activity feed from PreToolUse hooks, desk-handoff button (defer + release for claude --resume).
build_phases.deliverable: The phone shows what the IDE is doing (open project, active file, every terminal and its state) and covers non-tmux terminals as far as the platform allows; token revocation and audit review are one tap; a phone session hands off cleanly to the desk CLI.

risks: Concurrent resume of the same Claude session by CLI and daemon is UNVERIFIED — the design assumes single-writer JSONL and enforces exclusive attach with defer-based handoff; if the assumption is wrong in a subtle way, transcript corruption is possible.

Sessions run inside the VS Code Claude chat panel are permanently invisible (webview isolation, no exported API verified) — the product mitigates by making daemon/CLI-in-tmux the steered default, but a user who lives in the chat panel gets nothing.

Killed-state notification action taps are the least reliable path on both platforms (Android no-op history, iOS background-JS edge cases); mitigated by idempotent decisions, expiry, escalating re-notify, and tap-to-open fallback — but 'approve from lock screen' will occasionally degrade to 'open the app'.

Anthropic SDK churn: the V2 session API was already removed once (0.3.142); canUseTool/hook semantics could shift under a personal-subscription auth model, and Agent SDK usage against a Claude subscription vs API billing is a cost/ToS detail to verify before Phase 1.

ACP maturity: Gemini/Codex adapter quality and optional capabilities vary; cold-restart recovery is community-reported weak, so the daemon's own transcript mirror is load-bearing, and Codex adapter behavior may lag Codex releases.

Ops fragility of a home server: laptop sleep, Tailscale key expiry, TestFlight 90-day build expiry, and tailscale-serve cert renewal are four independent ways the system dies silently while traveling — setup automation and a daemon self-health push reduce but don't eliminate this.

Shell-integration mirroring silently fails on nonstandard zsh configs (powerlevel10k instant prompt is a known offender) and is attach-at-start-only — Phase 4's non-tmux coverage is genuinely best-effort.
tmux wrapper only covers terminals opened after setup; pre-existing shells and deliberate non-tmux terminals stay dark, which the UI must keep saying honestly.
Expo Push is a third-party dependency in the critical alert path (metadata-only exposure, but availability matters); an outage means delayed approvals with no self-hosted fallback built.

Recurring costs/chores are structural: $99/yr Apple, Android developer-verification signup when enforcement reaches the region, and solo maintenance of three artifacts (daemon, app, extension) against moving targets — the Omnara lesson is why every agent integration sits on structured protocols, not TUI scraping.
not_built: No relay server or hosted backend — Tailscale WireGuard direct replaces the entire Happy-style relay + E2E-crypto layer (and its Discussion-#680 class of key-custody bugs).
No custom push infrastructure — Expo Push Service fronts APNs/FCM; payloads are content-free so nothing sensitive is entrusted to it.
No terminal emulator or multiplexer — xterm.js/@xterm/headless and tmux are adopted wholesale; ttyd/GoTTY/upterm/VibeTunnel are studied for architecture but not used as components.
No TUI scraping or PTY wrapping of agents — approvals and streaming come only from Agent SDK and ACP structured channels; the tmux mirror is a dumb screen, never parsed.
No Claude chat-panel integration and no onDidWriteTerminalData dependency — both are platform dead ends; at most the extension focuses the panel.
No codex exec path (zero approval prompts) and no ACP-only architecture (Claude gets the richer native SDK).
No generic shell-exec API endpoint — typed operations only; the security boundary is API shape.
No App Store / Play Store release, no multi-user accounts, no web client, no voice — one user, TestFlight + sideload.
No full-IDE-on-phone feature — 'code tunnel' to vscode.dev is documented as an escape hatch, not productized.
No custom session persistence for Claude — the shared ~/.claude/projects store is the database of record for transcripts; SQLite only holds events, approvals, auth, and ACP mirrors.

name: Switchboard
thesis: The product IS the protocol: one laptop daemon defines a small internal wire protocol ("SBP") copied from ACP's shapes — session lifecycle, streamed updates with tool-call status (pending/in_progress/completed/failed), permission requests with the four ACP option kinds (allow_once/allow_always/reject_once/reject_always), plus two extensions ACP lacks (raw terminal frames, per-session cursor sequence numbers) — and every surface plugs in through a SurfaceAdapter that normalizes to it: Claude via the native Agent SDK, other agents via a single generic ACP client, plain terminals via tmux control mode, VS Code via a thin sensor extension. The phone app is a dumb SBP client over Tailscale that renders sessions by declared capability flags, so adding Gemini/Codex/any future ACP agent is a config entry, not an app change. ACP is the interop bet the research validates (Gemini native, official claude-agent-acp and codex-acp adapters, JetBrains adoption suite-wide), and modeling the internal schema on it is exactly the researchers' recommendation ("normalize all tiers into one event schema modeled on ACP's shapes"). Deliberately NOT ACP-only for Claude, per the same research: canUseTool/updatedPermissions/AskUserQuestion, the defer-hook restart path, and the shared ~/.claude/projects store are higher-fidelity than the ACP mapping.
laptop_side: Two components. (1) `swbd` daemon — Node 26 (already installed) + TypeScript, installed as a launchd LaunchAgent (must be a user agent, not a LaunchDaemon, or it lands on the wrong tmux socket per the tmux research). Stack: Fastify for the typed HTTP API + `ws` for the SBP WebSocket, bound ONLY to the laptop's Tailscale 100.x address; TLS terminated by `tailscale serve` (auto-renewed ts.net Let's Encrypt cert). Core: better-sqlite3 append-only event log — every SBP event gets a per-session monotonic seq, which is what makes reconnect-and-catch-up work; approvals, decisions, and an audit log of every mutating call live in the same DB. Adapter host loads four adapters behind the SurfaceAdapter interface: ClaudeAdapter (@anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk `query()` with includePartialMessages throttled/batched before the wire, canUseTool for approvals, PermissionRequest hook to fire push, cwd pinned per session, PreToolUse hook feeding an auto-approved activity feed; built on query()+options only — the V2 createSession API was removed in 0.3.142); AcpAdapter (@agentclientprotocol/sdk client spawning any binary declared in ~/.config/switchboard/agents.toml as a stdio subprocess; implements the CLIENT-side terminal capability via node-pty since ACP puts terminals on the client; feature-detects loadSession/resume and keeps its own transcript mirror in SQLite because ACP cold-restart recovery is unreliable); TmuxAdapter (`tmux -C attach` control-mode client hosted on node-pty against the default per-user socket — sees ALL user tmux sessions including manually started ones; capture-pane -p -e -S - for connect-time replay, %output stream with octal-unescape to raw bytes, send-keys for input, refresh-client -f pause-after for flow control, and it NEVER issues refresh-client -C so the phone can never resize a pane — Claude Code's ink TUI demonstrably corrupts on resize; @xterm/headless + serialize addon per watched pane for instant reconnect snapshots); VscodeAdapter (a localhost WS endpoint the extension dials out to). Plus Expo Push sender, QR pairing endpoint, and a `swb` CLI (`swb claude`, `swb sh`) that starts sessions through the daemon from any laptop terminal. (2) `switchboard-vscode` — thin Marketplace-legal companion extension, pure sensor/actuator (details under surface_capture). Setup prerequisites: `brew install tmux`, pmset prevent-sleep-when-plugged-in, Tailscale node key expiry disabled day one.
phone_side: Expo (React Native + TypeScript) with expo-dev-client — NOT a PWA and NOT Expo Go: iOS web push has no action buttons and materially worse delivery, and Expo Go cannot receive remote push. Distribution: paid Apple Developer Program ($99/yr, non-negotiable for APNs) + TestFlight internal testing (90-day re-upload on a calendar/CI reminder); Android via EAS-built APK sideload, registering the free 20-device limited-distribution account ahead of the Sept 2026 verification enforcement. Libraries: expo-notifications (an "approval" category with Approve + Deny-with-text-input actions, opensAppToForeground:false, time-sensitive interruption level, graceful degrade if the user disables it), expo-secure-store behind Face ID for the device token, Shopify FlashList for agent transcripts and logs (cheap, copyable, searchable — never xterm for chat streams), and an xterm.js-in-WebView terminal view following the @fressh/react-native-xtermjs-webview pattern (rAF + 8KB write coalescing across the bridge, custom accessory key row for Ctrl/Esc/Tab/arrows) reserved for real PTY sessions, rendered at the pane's laptop-side column width with pan/pinch — never resized to phone width. App structure, five screens: Sessions list (grouped by surface, honest capability badges from SBP flags: "controllable", "structured approvals", "mirror only", "observed, best-effort", "not capturable"); Approvals inbox ("waiting on you", full tool input/diff cards with the four option kinds + steering text); Session detail (FlashList chat renderer for agent sessions, xterm renderer for terminals); New Task; Devices & Settings (pairing QR scanner, device revocation, audit view). Connection model: one WSS while foregrounded, torn down on background (iOS suspends apps and background URLSession has no WebSockets — the daemon must never treat socket-drop as user-gone), full catch-up from last-seen cursor on every resume; every push is a signal carrying only IDs, with authoritative state fetched on open.
transport: Tailscale-direct on the free Personal plan (laptop + phone = 2 devices, 1 user). Daemon binds the tailnet interface only — home-Wi-Fi devices cannot even reach the port; `tailscale serve` fronts it with a real Let's Encrypt cert on laptop.<tailnet>.ts.net so the Expo app gets clean HTTPS/WSS with zero ATS exceptions and automatic 90-day renewal (raw `tailscale cert` files would expire mid-trip). iPhone uses VPN On Demand with the *.ts.net hostname trigger (interface rule "Do Nothing") so the tunnel auto-establishes when the app dials the MagicDNS name; the app builds in connect-retry because the first request after tunnel-down can time out. Tailscale is a device-wide VPN, so the RN app needs no SDK embedding; no exit node means no battery problem. Laptop node key expiry disabled on day one (180-day default silently kills reachability). On top of WireGuard: QR-code pairing hands the phone a per-device random bearer token, stored hashed on the laptop, individually revocable in a device list; the API is typed operations only — approve(approvalId, optionId), sendPrompt(sessionId), terminalInput(sessionId), startSession(agent, dir ∈ allowlisted roots) — never a generic exec endpoint; every mutating call is audit-logged. Why not the alternatives: Cloudflare Tunnel's edge terminates TLS and reads the plaintext command channel, and a service token in the app is a static long-lived credential; a self-hosted relay is an internet-facing service to patch forever and the Happy #680 finding (server-decryptable "E2E" API keys) shows how that goes wrong. Result: zero public endpoints, zero relays, WireGuard E2E by default. The single outbound-only exception is push (below).
surface_capture: (1) CLAUDE CODE SESSIONS — three tiers, shown honestly. Daemon-hosted (the steered path): started via `swb claude` or from the phone; ClaudeAdapter runs query() with includePartialMessages for streaming and canUseTool for structured approvals; sessions land in the shared ~/.claude/projects/<encoded-cwd>/ store, so `claude --resume <id>` on the laptop picks up phone-started work — attach is treated as EXCLUSIVE (single-writer JSONL, concurrent resume behavior unverified): the daemon releases the session before a laptop resume and vice versa. CLI-started sessions the daemon didn't host: listed read-only via SDK listSessions()/getSessionMessages() with a "take over via resume" action once the CLI exits; if the user ran claude inside tmux, they additionally get a live exact-screen mirror + keystroke steering via the TmuxAdapter (no structured approvals — approval detection by TUI scraping is explicitly rejected as the Omnara maintenance treadmill). Sessions inside the VS Code Claude chat panel: NOT capturable — webview isolation is absolute; they may surface read-only through the projects store [UNVERIFIED] and otherwise show as "not capturable". (2) OTHER AI AGENTS — one generic AcpAdapter covers all of them: Gemini CLI (`--experimental-acp`, native ACP) and Codex (via the official @agentclientprotocol/codex-acp package — never `codex exec`, which has zero approval prompts) declared in agents.toml; session/request_permission maps 1:1 onto the approvals inbox, session/update onto streaming; the daemon implements ACP's client-side terminal methods with node-pty so agent shell commands stream live; own transcript mirror kept because session/load is unreliable cold-recovery. Any future ACP agent is a new agents.toml entry. (3) PLAIN TERMINALS — tmux is the single capture layer: TmuxAdapter sees every session on the user's default socket regardless of who started tmux; connect-time scrollback via capture-pane -p -e -S -, live bytes via %output (octal-unescaped before feeding xterm.js, since payloads can split UTF-8/ANSI sequences), input via send-keys, pause-mode flow control so a `yarn build` can't flood LTE, history-limit set before spawning. VS Code's default terminal profile is switched to `tmux new -A -s vscode-N` so user-opened IDE terminals are captured and crash-persistent for free. Non-tmux terminals cannot be retro-attached (PTY masters are owned by VS Code's ptyHost; reptyr doesn't support macOS) — the UI says "not capturable" instead of pretending. (4) VS CODE ITSELF — the companion extension is a pure sensor/actuator dialing out to the daemon on localhost: reports IDE state (workspace.workspaceFolders, activeTextEditor, tabGroups, window focus, terminal inventory with TerminalState.shell + processId + cwd) as an IDE-presence card; best-effort mirrors user terminals via the stable shell-integration API (subscribe in onDidStartTerminalShellExecution, call execution.read() immediately — attach-at-start-only, command-scoped, silently absent on p10k-style zsh configs, so it degrades to "input-only"); injects input via Terminal.sendText with shouldExecute:false for raw keys, with the daemon verifying terminal identity before routing phone input. Never built on onDidWriteTerminalData (forever-proposed, Marketplace-blocked) and never touches the Claude chat webview. One extension host per window: the daemon namespaces multiple extension connections.
approvals_flow: 1. BLOCK: ClaudeAdapter's canUseTool fires (only for non-auto-approved tools — an allow rule or acceptEdits bypasses silently, so a PreToolUse hook logs those to the activity feed instead) or an ACP agent sends session/request_permission; the returned promise/JSON-RPC reply is held open — the agent is genuinely paused. 2. NORMALIZE: daemon writes an Approval record {approvalId, sessionId, toolName, input/diff, optionKinds[], createdAt} to the event log with a fresh cursor seq; state=pending; the PermissionRequest hook (documented exactly for this) triggers step 3. 3. NOTIFY: content-free Expo push — category "approval", time-sensitive, payload carries only IDs, "A session needs your approval". Lock screen shows Approve / Deny (Deny with a text-input steering field). 4. ACT, path A (lock screen): action handler runs with opensAppToForeground:false, the *.ts.net dial auto-raises the Tailscale tunnel if down, and POSTs the idempotent, approvalId-scoped decision with retry/backoff; a local confirmation notification replaces the original. Path B (guaranteed fallback, since killed-state actions are the least reliable path on both platforms): tapping the body deep-links to the Approvals inbox, which shows the full tool-input/diff card and all four option kinds (allow_once, allow_always → returned as updatedPermissions for Claude, reject_once, reject_always) plus an optional steering message. Path C (laptop): nothing changes — but any decision made anywhere is an event on the cursor log, so phone and laptop converge. 5. RESUME: daemon validates the device token, appends the decision to the audit log, and resolves the held call — canUseTool returns {behavior:'allow', updatedInput, updatedPermissions?} or {behavior:'deny', message: steeringText}; ACP gets its request_permission response. The agent continues; the stream flows; the inbox card flips to resolved via WS or next cursor catch-up. 6. HARDENING: unanswered approvals re-notify on an escalating schedule (push receipts prove handoff to APNs, not delivery); if the daemon must restart with an approval pending, the Claude defer-hook decision lets the process exit and the approval is re-raised on session resume, so the prompt is never lost; decisions are idempotent with server-side expiry so double-taps and stale actions are no-ops.
notifications: Pipeline: daemon → HTTPS POST to Expo Push Service (free, outbound-only — no public endpoint on the laptop, and no APNs certificate plumbing to maintain) → APNs/FCM → device. Two categories: "approval" (actions as above) and "attention" (session finished, errored, went idle waiting for input, ACP agent asked a question). All payloads are content-free (IDs + generic text) because they transit Expo and APNs in plaintext and APNs caps at 4KB anyway — the app fetches real content over the tunnel. iOS interruption level time-sensitive (self-service capability, breaks through Focus), degrading to normal if the user disables it. Requires the paid Apple Developer Program; Expo push-security access tokens enabled and the ExponentPushToken treated as a secret; DeviceNotRegistered receipts rotate stored tokens. Delivery honesty: a ticket is not delivery, so every notified event is ALSO always visible in the in-app inbox, and unanswered approvals re-notify. Android action-button handling in killed state gets on-device testing in week one (historically buggy in expo-notifications despite the 2025 fix). No silent/content-available pushes for sync — foreground cursor catch-up plus visible pushes only.
remote_start: Phone "New Task" screen → GET /projects returns the allowlisted project roots from ~/.config/switchboard/config.toml (the daemon scans one level under each root for directories; nothing outside the allowlist is ever startable — this is the API-shape security control, not a command filter). User picks a directory, then a surface: (a) Claude — daemon starts a ClaudeAdapter query() with cwd pinned to that directory (resume is keyed to encoded cwd, and resuming from the wrong dir silently forks a fresh session, so the daemon owns cwd per session) and the user's typed prompt as the first message; the session is later resumable on the laptop with `claude --resume <id>`. (b) Any ACP agent from agents.toml — daemon spawns the binary in that directory and forwards the prompt as the first session/prompt. (c) Plain shell — `tmux new-session -d -c <dir>` on the user socket; the new pane appears in the sessions list and, because it's plain tmux, is equally attachable from the laptop (`tmux attach`) — two-way by construction. Typed input into a spawned shell is inherently remote command execution; it rides the same pairing + hashed-token + audit-log controls, and terminal input is logged keystroke-for-keystroke. The daemon runs as a LaunchAgent with the laptop configured not to sleep while plugged in, so remote start works with the lid closed and no terminal open — the Happy-daemon pattern, rebuilt on our protocol.

build_phases.scope: SBP schema + better-sqlite3 cursor event log; Fastify/ws daemon as LaunchAgent bound to the tailnet; tailscale serve TLS; QR pairing + hashed device tokens + audit log; ClaudeAdapter (query, includePartialMessages throttled, canUseTool, PermissionRequest hook, cwd pinning, defer-on-restart); `swb claude` CLI wrapper; Expo dev-client app with Sessions list, Approvals inbox, FlashList transcript, prompt send; Expo push with approval category and killed-state action testing on real devices; EAS + TestFlight setup. Day-one spikes: verify SDK-CLI session-store interop and lock-screen actions, since both are load-bearing.
build_phases.deliverable: Start a Claude session in any project with `swb claude`, walk away, get a time-sensitive push when it blocks, approve/deny/steer from the lock screen or inbox, and watch the live stream from anywhere — the core pain is gone.

build_phases.scope: New Task screen; allowlisted project roots; startSession typed op; session finished/errored/idle 'attention' pushes with escalating re-notify; read-only listing of CLI-started Claude sessions via listSessions()/getSessionMessages() with take-over-via-resume; exclusive-attach handoff both directions; Devices screen with revocation.
build_phases.deliverable: Kick off new Claude work on any project from the phone with the laptop lid closed, get told when it finishes, and hand sessions between laptop CLI and phone.

build_phases.scope: brew install tmux + pmset setup script; TmuxAdapter (control-mode client, capture-pane replay, %output octal decode, send-keys, pause-mode flow control, no-resize invariant); @xterm/headless serialize snapshots; xterm.js WebView renderer with write coalescing, key accessory row, pan/zoom at laptop pane width; VS Code default-profile tmux wrapper; tmux new-session remote spawn.
build_phases.deliverable: Every tmux terminal on the laptop — including ones started manually and inside VS Code — is watchable and drivable from the phone, with an exact-screen mirror of any TUI (including interactive claude) as the fallback view.

build_phases.scope: AcpAdapter on @agentclientprotocol/sdk; agents.toml registry; Gemini CLI --experimental-acp and Codex via @agentclientprotocol/codex-acp; capability feature-detection; client-side terminal methods via node-pty; SQLite transcript mirror; permission/update mapping onto the existing inbox and stream.
build_phases.deliverable: Gemini and Codex sessions sit in the same list and same approvals inbox as Claude; any future ACP agent is a config entry.

build_phases.scope: switchboard-vscode extension: outbound localhost WS, IDE-state card (workspace, active file, tabs, focus, terminal inventory with shell/PID/cwd), best-effort shell-integration output mirror with input-only degradation, sendText actuation with terminal-identity verification, multi-window namespacing.
build_phases.deliverable: The phone shows what the IDE is doing and can nudge non-tmux user terminals; the honest capability badges now cover every surface on the machine.

risks: SDK<->CLI shared session store and `claude --resume` interop is consistent with the docs but flagged UNVERIFIED beyond the brief, and concurrent two-writer resume is explicitly UNVERIFIED — Phase 2 handoff depends on it; mitigated by a day-one spike and by treating attach as strictly exclusive, but if interop breaks, phone-started sessions become daemon-only.

This deliberately rebuilds ~90% of Happy (MIT, 22.9k stars) for protocol purity plus unified terminals; the payoff is longevity and the terminal gap Happy lacks, the cost is that one person owns a daemon, a protocol, four adapters, and a mobile app forever — Omnara's deprecation shows what happens when maintenance outruns motivation (partially mitigated: nothing here scrapes a TUI, the brittleness that killed Omnara).

Killed-state notification actions are the least reliable path on both platforms (Android no-op history in expo-notifications, iOS background-JS edge cases); if they flake, lock-screen approve degrades to tap-to-open-inbox — annoying but functional.
Apple treadmill: $99/yr, TestFlight builds expire every 90 days, push entitlement paperwork; a missed re-upload bricks the app mid-trip. Needs a CI cron.

ACP is young: Gemini's flag is literally named --experimental-acp, cold-restart session recovery is community-reported as weak, and per-agent capabilities vary — the SQLite transcript mirror and feature detection contain this, but Tier-2 agents will always be lower-fidelity than Claude.

The daemon is a single point of failure holding pending canUseTool promises; the defer-hook + resume path covers Claude, but ACP has no equivalent — a daemon crash mid-approval on an ACP agent loses that prompt (agent must be re-prompted).

Anything not in tmux and not started by the daemon is invisible or best-effort by hard platform limits (no macOS PTY re-attach, shell-integration attach-at-start-only, forever-proposed raw-data API, Claude chat panel webview isolation) — the design is honest about it in the UI, but the user must adopt the tmux-wrapper habit to get coverage.

Laptop environmental failures are the most likely real-world outage: sleep (pmset/caffeinate misconfig), Tailscale node key expiry (must disable day one), or the LaunchAgent dying silently — needs a heartbeat push ('laptop unreachable since…') in the app.
Whether VS Code Claude-panel sessions appear in ~/.claude/projects for read-only listing is UNVERIFIED; worst case that surface is fully dark and users must launch agents via swb/phone.

The typed-API surface keeps remote exec constrained, but terminal input is still arbitrary command execution by design; a stolen unlocked phone within the tailnet window is the real threat — Face ID gate on the app, per-device revocation, and the audit log are the controls, and they must actually ship in Phase 1, not later.
not_built: No relay server and no custom E2E crypto layer — Tailscale WireGuard + ts.net TLS replaces the entire Happy-style relay tier (and avoids the Happy #680 class of bug by having no server to trust).
No TUI scraping for approval detection, ever — structured approvals come only from canUseTool and ACP request_permission; tmux capture is strictly an exact-screen mirror (the Omnara lesson).
No terminal transport of our own — tmux control mode + xterm.js instead of adopting or reimplementing ttyd/GoTTY/upterm/VibeTunnel, which solve public sharing, not private mirroring.
No push infrastructure — Expo Push Service fronts APNs/FCM; no APNs certs, no FCM server, no ntfy dependency (known-flaky for exactly this use case).
No Claude chat-panel integration in VS Code (webview isolation makes it impossible; at most a 'focus panel' command later) and no dependence on proposed VS Code APIs.
No generic shell-exec endpoint and no command allowlist theater — the API is typed operations with an allowlisted-directory start flow.

No replacement for Claude Code's built-in /remote-control — it stays documented as the zero-maintenance Claude-only fallback when Switchboard is down (noting it silently disables under DISABLE_TELEMETRY/DO_NOT_TRACK/custom base URLs).
No mobile IDE — `code tunnel` / vscode.dev in the phone browser is a documented escape hatch, not a component.

No App Store release, no multi-user support, no Android Play distribution — personal TestFlight + sideload only; if it ever goes multi-user, transport switches to a Happy-model E2E relay rather than inviting others into the tailnet.
No Codex `codex exec` path (zero approval prompts) and no dependence on the removed SDK V2 createSession API or archived zed-industries adapter repos.
No xterm rendering of agent chat streams (FlashList text is cheaper and better UX) and no PTY resizing to phone width anywhere in the system.
